name: Lablab (Dolichos bean)
harvestProduct: green pods / dry beans (food) and fodder / green-manure biomass (cover)

evidence.quote: Regarding extreme climatic conditions, lablab has a low tolerance for frost, especially because this plant can seed late.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 20: Lablab, SA Grain/Grain SA (Truter, Dannhauser, Smith & Trytsman), 2019

evidence.quote: An acceptable seeding rate is 25 kg/ha. For fodder and grazing 15 kg/ha – 20 kg/ha seed can be planted in rows during October/November.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 20: Lablab, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: If harvested for fodder purposes, it should be harvested just prior to the flowering stage and when cut, it is essential to leave sufficient stubble at a height of 10 cm – 15 cm to ensure optimal regrowth.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 20: Lablab, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Harvest/termination event is 'just prior to flowering' — no numeric day-count from sowing found in any SA source. Further search checked: (1) Grain SA's own Conservation Agriculture Manual Chapter 5 (Cover crops) -- has a Dolichos/lablab paragraph (N-fixation, pH range, July-August sowing per an external lablablab.org page) but no flowering/termination day-count; (2) a KZN DARD-style search for an SA lablab agronomy trial found none; (3) a peer-reviewed PLOS ONE paper (Nord et al. 2020, 'Investigating the diverse potential of a multi-purpose legume, Lablab purpureus (L.) Sweet, for smallholder production in East Africa', DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0227739) explicitly measures 'maturity (days to 50% flowering)' across 14 lablab accessions in Tanzania, so the variable exists in the literature, but the actual per-accession day numbers are reported only in a figure/table that did not survive this session's HTML-to-text extraction (only the variable-definition sentences were recoverable, not the numeric results) -- and even if recovered, this is Tanzanian accession-trial data, not South African, so it was not force-fitted in as a headline figure. Recorded as a genuine, still-open gap rather than guessing or using an unverifiable number.

evidence.quote: It is advised that this crop be planted in rows and preferably with a spacing of 30 cm apart in the row and 45 cm between rows.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 20: Lablab, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Numerous research trials indicate seasonal yields of 2 tons – 6 tons of DM/ha in sub-humid sub-tropics, depending on the specific climatic conditions in which the crop is grown.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 20: Lablab, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Being a legume, it can fix atmospheric nitrogen to the extent of around 170 kg/ha besides leaving enough crop residues to enrich the soils with organic matter.
evidence.doc: Conservation Agriculture Manual, Chapter 5: Cover crops, Grain SA, 2016

varieties.name: Rongai
varieties.season: Long growing season; poor frost tolerance
varieties.note: Vigorous twining growth habit, restores soil fertility as green manure, good insect/disease resistance, poor frost tolerance.

evidence.quote: It is a late maturing, vigorous, herbaceous, annual or shortlived perennial legume. ... Poor frost tolerance
evidence.doc: Rongai | Dolichos product page, Barenbrug South Africa

zoneNotes.highveld: Low tolerance for frost, so not recommended where hard frost arrives before the crop has finished seeding.

gaps: No exact day-count from sowing to flowering/termination; only 'just prior to flowering' as the harvest cue -- checked Grain SA's CA manual (no day-count) and a peer-reviewed East African (Tanzania) lablab accession trial (Nord et al. 2020, PLOS ONE) which measures 'days to 50% flowering' but whose numeric results were not recoverable from the accessible text/figures in this pass, and which is not SA-specific in any case; see daysToHarvestRange.notes.

Grain SA's Chapter 5 quotes an external lablab-info website giving 'sowing done in July-August' which conflicts with the SA-specific Part 20 article's October/November window; the SA Grain Part 20 figure (SA-specific, peer-authored) was preferred and the July-August figure was not used.
Only one named SA cultivar (Rongai) found; no early- vs late-maturing comparison for lablab specifically.
summary: Sow window (Oct/Nov), row+in-row spacing (45cm/30cm), seed rate (15-30 kg/ha), biomass yield (2-6 t DM/ha) and N-fixation (~170 kg/ha) are all sourced from Grain SA's Part 20 article and the Grain SA CA manual. Missing only an exact days-to-harvest figure (only 'just before flowering' given) and a broader variety list.
